thread:
incbot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Detected route instability on Direct Connect for customer ZetaCorp (dx-02-usa). Multiple BGP path flaps between us-east-2a and partner-router-3 causing partial traffic blackholing. Pagerduty triggered -> paging oncall

eng_dispatcher: Paging @sara_oncall and @alex_ops — severity P1. Customer portal shows 30% of requests failing with 504s since ~21:12 UTC.

sara_oncall: On it. I see notification from provider that one DX fiber in LAG is flapping. Looking at BGP sessions now.

alex_ops: I can confirm BGP flaps. Routes to ZetaCorp prefixes are oscillating between DX-peerA (AS65001) and DX-peerB (AS65002). Some prefixes are intermittently withdrawn.

paul_net: Attaching quick capture from our sflow at edge. Looks like ECMP path selection is bouncing when peerA withdraws briefly, AWS chooses peerB which has a partial route set -> traffic to some subnets ends up with no next-hop.

mike_cloud: From AWS side, Direct Connect LAG reports: 
```
LAG dx-02-usa: interfaces: 2/4 active, 1/4 admin-down, 1/4 flapping
BGP state: peerA (up/down flapping), peerB (up)
```

zeta_oncall: We're seeing client errors and some customers reporting API calls timing out. Impacting their ingestion pipelines. They're asking for ETA.

incbot: PagerDuty: incident created PD-5682 (oncall: sara_oncall). Escalation level 1.

sara_oncall: Immediate mitigations: 1) Announce to Zeta that we're working and enabling reroute via backup DX; 2) Disable ECMP on affected prefixes to prefer peerB until fiber stabilized; 3) Open ticket with DX provider for physical fiber. Planning to implement step 2 now.

alex_ops: Agree. I'll push a quick route-map to prefer peerB for ZetaCorp prefixes: 
```
route-map PREFER_PEERB permit 10
 set ip next-hop <peerB-next-hop>
!
apply to BGP neighbor peerA outbound for specific prefix-list ZETA_PREFIXES
```
This will force traffic away from the flapping peerA rather than bouncing ECMP.

paul_net: Caveat — that will steer all traffic via peerB and could increase load there. We should watch CPU on the DX-router and AWS VGW. I'll stand by for metrics.

mike_cloud: I can spin up temporary EC2 NAT accelerators in us-east-2 to handle overflow if peerB saturates. Standby to deploy if we see CPU > 70% or throughput > baseline 1.2x.

sara_oncall: Deploying route-map now. Applying to edge routers (rolling).

alex_ops: Route-map applied to core-edge-1 and core-edge-2. Confirming BGP updates propagated to AWS.

incbot: System: BGP route change detected at 21:26 UTC, 12 prefixes now preferred via peerB.

zeta_oncall: Confirmed significant reduction in 504s on our side. Thanks. Customers still seeing a few failing regions but overall much better.

paul_net: Monitoring: BGP flaps frequency dropped after steering, but fiber still shows intermittent errors. Provider maintenance ticket opened: TKT-9929 (fiber diagnostics).

sara_oncall: Noted. Next steps: 1) Keep steering until provider confirms hardware repaired; 2) Prepare rollback plan to re-enable ECMP if peerB becomes overloaded; 3) Notify account team and CSM to prepare customer comms.

mike_cloud: Deployed 2x t3.medium NAT instances as temporary egress. No sign of saturation. Throughput at ~60% expected baseline.

eng_dispatcher: CSM alerted @zeta_oncall, they acknowledged. Internal SRE postmortem block created: PM-2718. Please drop logs and config diffs there.

alex_ops: Saving config and diff: 
```
# diff before/after
- neighbor peerA route-map NONE out
+ neighbor peerA route-map PREFER_PEERB out (for ZETA_PREFIXES)
```

paul_net: Reminder: add a BGP dampening threshold check later. This oscillation was amplified by ECMP path bouncing. Could add MED/AS prepending as alternative.

zeta_oncall: Customer asked about permanent mitigation. Can we propose LAG health checks or use cross-connect redundancy? They want an ops doc to avoid recurrence.

sara_oncall: We'll include recommendations in postmortem: 1) Increase DX redundancy (additional cross-connect), 2) Use BGP prepending + community to steer during flaps, 3) Implement automated failover at the fabric edge with health-based routing policies.

incbot: :white_check_mark: RESOLUTION: At 21:44 UTC traffic stabilized with route steering. Provider scheduled field tech for 23:10 UTC. Incident state: mitigated (customer impact reduced). PD incident PD-5682 remains open until provider confirms repair.

eng_dispatcher: Handoff: @sara_oncall will continue any follow-ups with provider; @alex_ops to file config change request CL-4491 for permanent traffic engineering. Please update PM-2718 with timeline.

sara_oncall: Handoff acknowledged. I'll monitor BGP for 2 hours and update once ticket closed by provider. :alarm_clock:

zeta_oncall: Appreciated. We'll send an interim customer note stating mitigation and expected resolution window.

paul_net: Adding action item: run a controlled test tomorrow to validate failover behavior before business hours.

mike_cloud: I'll remove temp NATs once we confirm stable routes (post-provider confirmation).

incbot: Note: last message logged at 21:57 UTC.

sara_oncall: Closing conversation for now; will reopen if provider reports regression. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
